summary: SessionsClient.list() fetches /sessions and validates the wire shape the way ExternalToolsClient.get() does (isRecord + Array.isArray + every-element guard), so an unreachable backend or a row missing name is 'unavailable' and the client never throws. watch() opens new EventSource(`/sessions/${id}/stream`), reads bytes out of each message frame, and tells a data-carrying error frame (onFailure) from a dead connection (onUnreachable) the way plan-events/client.ts does -- the Sessions contract has no onRefused, so unlike PlanEventsClient there is no third branch: session-not-live is answered as a plain 400 before the SSE headers are ever written, so the browser's EventSource only ever sees it as a connection failure with no body, which lands on onUnreachable. type() posts {text} as json and does not interpret the response, matching the contract's Promise<void>. useLiveSessions wraps SessionsClient.list() in one effect with a mount-guard against a late resolution after unmount, starting at 'loading' and ending at 'loaded' or 'unavailable' -- no retry surface, since the contract exports only the state and the brief did not ask for one (useExternalTools's retry `check` has no equivalent here). vite.config.ts gained '/sessions' as a ninth proxied prefix; the stream and the input hang off it because vite proxies by path prefix. All seven tests from the brief's TDD/Tests lines were written first and watched fail on module-not-found before the implementation existed. One judgment call worth flagging: ct's style.md says every function hangs off a type, but every existing frontend client (external-tools, plan-events, start-plan, implement-plan, review-plan, active-plans, implement-history, implement-progress) is a set of module-level const functions grouped into one exported plain object, never a class -- I followed that same shape for SessionsClient/useLiveSessions per the brief's explicit 'Files to imitate', since deviating to a class would make this the only frontend client that does not match its own siblings; if that established idiom is itself considered a style.md gap, it is a slice-wide one, not something this task can fix alone.

Left unfixed this broke 45 tests across 5 files in three distinct ways: (a) a router that reuses one already-resolved Response or a single shared pending Promise for every unmatched URL handed that same object to both /sessions and the real request under test, and the second `.json()` read threw 'Body is unusable: Body has already been read'; (b) tests asserting on `fetching.mock.calls[0]` or `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` against a router that funnels every unmatched call through one shared jest.fn had their sequence/count thrown off by the extra call; (c) when a test genuinely simulates the whole backend being down, SessionsPanel's own Banner (role=alert, or role=status while merely loading) now coexists with Home's own alert/status banner, so a bare `findByRole('alert'|'status')` with no `name` matched either one non-deterministically.
